McDermott’s Hornpipe

This tune is very familiar but it isn’t like any McDermott’s tunes that already here so I suspect it has another name?

I lifted it from the Jim McKillop LP - ‘Mist in the Glen’.

↳ Posted by Ptarmigan on October 28th, 2005.

It’s certainly not the same McDermott’s which Andy McGann plays on ‘It’s a Hard Road to Travel’.

↳ Posted by Ptarmigan on October 28th, 2005.

A Google search on the first measure turned up the following at http://www.ibiblio.org/fiddlers/Mc_MEN.htm :

McDERMOT’S NO. 2. Irish, Hornpipe. Similar to the “Flowers of Antrim [1],” “Marquis of Lorne [1],” “Sligo Fancy” family of tunes. The tune is sometimes considered the last parts of a four-part hornpipe recorded in 1922 by New York/County Sligo fiddler Michael Coleman under the name “McDermott’s,” a name which has stuck. The first two parts of the Coleman piece are also called “The Galway Hornpipe [1]” or “The Baldheaded Bachelor.”

T:McDermot’s No. 2
R:hornpipe
S:A homemade tape of Con Cassidy of unknown provenance
Z:Transcribed by Larry Sanger

Sorcha Costelloe’s McDermott’s (Flowers of Antrim)

Setting #3, which I’ll add momentarily, is my transcription of Sorcha Costelloe’s playing of McDermott’s Hornpipe #2, aka Flowers of Antrim, from this Comhaltas Live video of her 2nd place performance in the 2013 All-Ireland Fleadh. I think I got most, if not all, of the long rolls, but omitted the short rolls. I’m not sure about the double stops (and I left a few out) so if anyone can point out the errors, I’ll fix them.
http://comhaltas.ie/music/detail/comhaltaslive_435_6_sorcha_costello/

↳ Posted by GaryAMartin on May 5th, 2014.

Re: McDermott’s

This tune is the one I know as ‘The Marquis of Lorne’ (with a setting in G in the Kennedy ‘Fiddlers’ Tune Book’).

On Andy McGann’s ‘Hard Road to Travel’ LP, he plays once through a different one under the title of ‘McDermott’s’, then goes into this one, and adds one called ‘From Galway to Dublin’ - which I think is similar to ‘Napoleon crossing the Rhine’ but perhaps not the same tune.

↳ Posted by Bazza on July 31st, 2017.

Re: McDermott’s

For anyone who would look for the exact order of the tunes in Andy McGann’s set (which can be deduced from the above comments but I’m putting it there for the sake of clarity) :
[[The Galway/McDermott’s (The Marquis of Lorne)/The Galway/This setting of The Marquis of Lorne]] => considered by Coleman and McGann as a 4-part hornpipe
=> then From Galway to Dublin (Bonaparte Crossing the Rhine).

Here is a link to Michael Coleman’s 1922 OKeh recording (oh the wonders you can find on the Internet) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fCNcoPZzPyA
